topics.title: Mathematics second term Scheme of work for Nigeria junior secondary school (JSS1 - JSS3) students.
topics.content:
Mathematics second term Scheme of work for Nigeria junior secondary school (JSS1 - JSS3) students.
JSS1: Second Term’s Scheme of Work
Week 1: APPROXIMATION
i. Obtaining approximate
values for calculation involving four basic arithmetic processes (operations).
ii. Rounding off of numbers
to the nearest 10, 100, 1000.
iii. Quantitative reasoning
involving approximation.
Week 2: OPEN SENTENCES
i. Use of letters to
represent numbers.
ii. Distinguishing between
open and closed sentences.
iii. Supplying the missing
numbers in open sentences from a set of given permissible substitutes.
Week 3: SIMPLIFYING ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSION
i. Identifying the
coefficient of symbols or letters.
ii. Distinguishing
algebraic expressions from non-algebraic expressions.
Week 4: SIMPLIFYING ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSION 2
i. Basic operation of
addition, substraction, multiplication and division of algebraic symbols and
terms.
ii. Collection of like
terms.
Week 5: WORD PROBLEMS
i. Formation of word
problems (simple cases).
ii. Word problems involving
uses of symbols.
iii. Quantitative reasoning
involving algebraic expressions.
Week 6: SIMPLE EQUATIONS IN ONE VARIABLE
i. Identifying simple
equations in one variable.
ii. Examples of three types
of equality - absolute, referential and conditional equality.
Week 7: DIRECTED NUMBERS
i. Addition and
substraction of numbers using number line.
ii. Use of number line.
Week 8: BASIC PROPERTIES OF SOME COMMON THREE DIMENSIONAL FIGURES
i. Basic properties of
cubes, cuboids, pyramids, cylinders, e.g., faces, vertices and edges.
Week 9: BASIC PROPERTIES OF SOME COMMON THREE DIMENSIONAL
DIMENSIONAL FIGURES 2
i. Sphere

ii. Cone
iii. Triangular prism,
e.g., faces, vertices and edges
Week 10: PROPERTIES OF FIGURES
i. Rectangles
ii. Square
iii. Isosceles triangles
iv. Equivalent triangles
v. Circles
Week 11/12: Revision/Examination
JSS2: Second Term’s Scheme of Work
Week 1: EXPANSION OF ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSION
i. Expansion of the form
a(b + c) = ab + ac
ii. Expansion of the form
(a + b) (c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd
iii. Quantitative reasoning
involving expansion
Week 2: FACTORIZATION OF ALGEBRAIC EXPRESSION
i. Factorisation of the
form ax + ay = a (x + y)
ii. Factorisation of the
form abc + abd = ab (c + d)
Week 3: ALGEBRAIC FRACTION
i. Algebraic fraction with
monomial denominators (addition, substraction, multiplication and division)
ii. Word problems leading
to simple algebraic fractions
Week 4: SIMPLE EQUATIONS
i. Solving simple equations
ii. Word problems on simple
equations.
Week 5: LINEAR INEQUALITIES IN ONE VARIABLE
i. Solution of linear
inequalities
ii. Graphical
representation of linear inequalities
iii. Word problems
involving linear inequalities in one variable
Week 6: PLANES, SHAPES AND FIGURES
Properties of:
i. Parallelogram
ii. Rhombus
iii. Kite
Week 7: ANGLES IN A POLYGON
i. Revision of angles in a
triangle
ii. Identification and
naming of polygons (up to 10 sides)
iii. Sum of angles in a
quadrilateral.
iv. The sum of interior
angles in a polygon
Week 8: SCALE DRAWING
i. Drawing plane objects to
scale
ii. Converting actual
lengths to scale
iii. Calculation from scale
drawing
iv. Combination of plane
shapes to produce design
Week 9: GRAPHS
i. Revision of plotting of
points on the Cartesian plane
ii. Solutions of linear
equations in two variables using graphs
iii. Linear graphs from
real life situations
Week 10: ANGLES OF ELEVATION AND DEPRESSION
i. Identifying angles of
elevation and depression
ii. Distinguishing between
angles of elevation and depression
iii. Measuring angles of
elevation and depression
iv. Using angles of
elevation and depression in calculating distances and heights
Week 11/12: Revision/Examination
JSS3: Second Term’s Scheme of Work
Week 1: CHANGE OF SUBJECT OF FORMULA
i. Changing subject in a
formula
ii. Simplifying expression
by substituting in formula
Week 2: COMPOUND INTEREST
i. Revision of simple
interest
ii. Solving problems on
compound interest
iii. Applying the use of
compound interest in daily life activities
Week 3: VIEWS, PLANS AND SKETCHES
Drawing views and plans of
common solids:
i. Cube and cuboids
ii. Cone
iii. Cylinder
iv. Sphere
v. Prism
Week 4: PROBABILITY
i. Define probability
ii. Use probability to
estimate the outcomes of real-life problems involving chance
iii. Express probability as
a fraction
iv. Determine the
probability of events such as throwing a die, picking a ball from a bag etc.
Week 5: SIMILAR SHAPES
a. Identify similar figures:
i. Triangles
ii. Rectangles
iii. Squares
iv. Cubes
b. Identifying the presence
of similar shapes in the environment
Week 6: ENLARGEMENT AND SCALE FACTOR
i. Meaning of enlargement
and scale factor
ii. Enlargement shapes
using scale factor
iii. Calculating and
comparing lengths, areas and volumes of similar figures
iv. Quantitative reasoning
involving similar shapes
Week 7: TRIGONOMETRY
i. Identify sine, cosine
and tangent of an acute angle as ratios of sides of a right-angled triangle
ii. Using trigonometric
ratio to solve practical problems
iii. Applying trigonometric
ratios to solve problems
Week 8: SOLID SHAPES
Problems in measuration
involving:
i. Volume of cylinders,
cones.
ii. Surface areas of
cylinder and cones.
Week 9: CONSTRUCTION
i. Bisecting of line
segment
ii. Bisecting of angles
iii. Constructing simple
shapes
Week 10: CONSTRUCTION 2
i. Construction of angles
of various sizes: 90°, 60°, 40°, 30°
ii. Copying a given angle
iii. Constructing simple
shapes
Week 11/12: Revision/Examination
